item.title: トランプ氏、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止を「非常に真剣に」検討
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は27日、物価高への対応として米国産ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止を導入する案について、引き続き「非常に真剣に」検討していると述べた。一方、政権内では別の対応策の検討も続いている。

トランプ氏はシカゴ近郊で開催されたゴルフのプレジデンツカップ最終日を観戦した際、FOXニュースの記者に「そう（ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止）すると自動車用ガソリン価格が若干上昇することがよくある。非常に真剣に検討しており、実施する可能性はある」と語った。

秋の収穫期が最盛期を迎えるなか、農業州選出の複数の議員はトランプ氏に対し、米国産ディーゼル燃料の輸出規制を求めている。世界の燃料市場では、要衝ホルムズ海峡を経由する物流の混乱や、ウクライナによるロシア製油所攻撃で大きな影響が出ている。米国は世界の最後の供給元となっており、ディーゼル燃料の輸出量は先月、週間ベースで過去最高となる日量200万バレル近くに急増した。

米国家経済会議（NEC）のハセット委員長、ベッセント米財務長官、グリア米通商代表部（USTR）代表はこの1週間、米国産ディーゼル燃料を短期間、輸出禁止とした場合の影響を分析している。政権がこの案を本格的に検討していることを示すものだ。

一方、石油会社の最高経営責任者（CEO）や業界団体は輸出禁止の代わりに、連邦政府が課すディーゼル燃料の物品税を一時停止するよう求めている。輸出禁止に伴う問題を生じさせずに価格を抑えられるとしている。ただ、下院が中間選挙前の休会に入っていることもあり、物品税の停止方法を巡って政権内で議論がある。

原題：Trump Says He’s ‘Very Seriously’ Looking at Diesel Export Ban（抜粋）

item.title: ヘッジファンドの人気取引に追い風、AI・原油巡り勝ち組と負け組
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： AIへの期待と不安が入り交じる中での個別株の激しい値動きや債券相場の急落、地政学的な混乱が、ヘッジファンド運用者が長年好んできた取引に追い風となっている。

メタ・プラットフォームズの新たなAIエージェント「Muse（ミューズ）」などの進歩を巡って期待が広がる一方、AI分野の急成長が銀行や旅行代理店など幅広い企業に打撃を与えるとの懸念も強まっており、株価は銘柄によって逆方向に動いている。イランやウクライナでの戦争を巡る相次ぐ報道も、石油生産会社と石油精製会社の株価を大きく揺さぶった。一方、米国債利回りは20年ぶりの高水準に達し、借り入れコストを押し上げた。

野村ホールディングスでフロー株式デリバティブ営業責任者を務めるアレックス・コソグリャドフ氏は「最近、顧客から問い合わせが増えているテーマの1つが、エージェント型AIを巡る勝ち組と負け組という構図だ」と述べ、「エージェント型AI革命の進展で恩恵を受けるのは誰か。あるいは、脅威にさらされるのは誰かという問いだ」と話した。

AI、原油、金利を巡って勝ち組と負け組が分かれる状況は、ディスパージョン取引（分散取引）に理想的な環境を生み出す。S&P500種株価指数のような指数の構成銘柄が異なる方向に動けば、指数自体の値動きは抑えられるためだ。

個別株のインプライド・ボラティリティー（IV、予想変動率）は7月下旬以降低下しており、特に大きく上昇してきたテクノロジー銘柄で顕著だ。このため、ディスパージョン取引を始める魅力が高まっている。

RBCキャピタル・マーケッツでフローデリバティブ取引担当ディレクターを務めるマシュー・デービス氏は「取引を始めるという観点では、個別株のボラティリティーが低下したため、少し前と比べれば相対的に割安になっている」と語った。

個別株とS&P500のボラティリティーの差は再び拡大し始めている。トレーダーは両者の乖離（かいり）から利益を得るため、個別株のオプションを買う一方、指数のオプションを売っている。決算発表シーズンが近づく中、この傾向は続く可能性がある。決算期には、何らかのマクロ要因を受けて株式が一斉に動くよりも、企業固有の材料に基づいて株価がそれぞれに動く傾向があるためだ。

item.title: 米国債が逆イールド接近、FRB利上げで景気冷え込みに警戒
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）： 米国債市場では、
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国債市場では、 米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）の一連の利上げを受け、市場の焦点が米景気失速のリスクへ移りつつあることを示す段階に近づいている。

米国債の10年物と2年物の利回り格差は先週、一時17ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）まで縮小し、2025年初め以来の低水準となった。イールドカーブのフラット化が進んでいることで、10年債利回りが近く短期債を下回る逆イールドとなる可能性が高まっている。

逆イールドはこれまで景気後退の有力な先行指標とされてきた。2020年代は予測が外れたものの、1960年代までさかのぼる直近8回のリセッション（景気後退）では逆イールドが先行した。インフレ抑制を目指すFRBが景気を冷やす水準まで金利を引き上げるとの市場の見方を映す。実際にそうなれば、金融市場全体、とりわけ最高値圏にある株式への影響が大きい。

FRBは今月、3年ぶりに利上げし、追加利上げの可能性も示した。インフレ抑制に向けた利上げが景気を冷やすシナリオに備える投資家が増えている。力強い景気を背景とする物価上昇圧力を映して債券売りが進んできたが、FRBがタカ派姿勢を強めるなか、リスクの構図が変わりつつあることも浮き彫りになっている。

調査会社クレジットサイツの投資適格債・マクロ戦略責任者、ザック・グリフィス氏は「2年債と10年債のイールドカーブが逆転したり、大幅にフラット化したりすれば、景気が非常に強いとの見方に疑問が生じる。債券市場は景気の強さへの疑念を一部織り込んでいる」と話す。

逆イールドになれば、24年以降に見られたイールドカーブの世界的な正常化が逆転する。債券投資家は、資金を長期にわたって投じることに伴う不確実性の見返りとして、より高い利回りを求める傾向がある。このため、イールドカーブは通常、右肩上がりになる。

先月までは、長期ゾーンの利回り急上昇を反映し、イールドカーブもスティープ化していた。ウォーシュFRB議長の下で、FRBのインフレ抑制への信認が低下するとの懸念も背景にあった。だが9月の利上げ後はより短期ゾーンの利回りが上昇。市場は今後1年間に少なくとも0.25ポイント利上げ3回分を織り込む。

item.title: アンソロピックのアモデイCEO、トランプ氏と夕食会へ
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米AI開発企業アンソロピックのダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（CEO）は27日夜、トランプ大統領と夕食を共にする予定だ。AIの安全性を巡る議論で対極に位置する2人が顔を合わせることになる。

アンソロピックのトップと政権との関係が数カ月にわたりぎくしゃくする中、今回の夕食会はアモデイ氏とトランプ氏が非公開で1対1の会談を行う初めての機会となる。両者の緊張は今年初め、国防総省との契約を巡る激しい対立で表面化し、6月に商務省がアンソロピックの画期的なAIモデル「Mythos（ミュトス）」に一時的に輸出規制を課したことで一段と深まった。

トランプ氏は27日、AIの新モデルの開発ペースを落とすよう求めたアモデイ氏の最近の主張について話し合う考えを示した。シカゴ近郊で開かれたゴルフトーナメントの会場で記者に対し、「それについて話すつもりだ」と述べ、「私は『前に進んで勝とう』という立場だ」と語った。

またAIの潜在力については、「実際、インターネットよりも大きな存在だ。われわれが先頭を走っており、何兆ドルもの施設を建設している。それをなぜ手放す必要があるのか」と話した。

夕食会については、非公開の予定であることを理由に複数の関係者も匿名で確認。米ニュースサイトのアクシオスが先に報じていた。アンソロピックとホワイトハウスの報道担当者は、コメントの要請に直ちに応じなかった。

今回の会談は、最先端のAIモデルによる注目度の高いセキュリティー侵害が相次ぎ、AIの安全性を巡る世界的な懸念が高まる中で行われる。アンソロピックの競合OpenAIは先週、同社のモデルが今年初めにオーストラリア政府のウェブサイトに不正侵入していたことを明らかにした。こうした事例を受け、米議員やテクノロジー業界の多くから新たなAI基準を求める声が強まっている。

アモデイ氏とトランプ氏は、AIがもたらす脅威について大きく異なる立場を示してきた。アモデイ氏は9月12日、AIが人類の存続にもたらすリスクを警告し、規制強化を求めるエッセーを発表し、AIの安全性を巡る議論を広く一般に浸透させた。また、最先端モデルの開発ペースを落とすと表明し、OpenAIのサム・アルトマンCEOとSpaceXAI創業者のイーロン・マスク氏もこれに賛同した。

item.title: 堺化学、おしろい材料で培った微粉末技術にAI特需－材料増産を検討
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 堺化学工業は、AIサーバー向け需要の拡大を受けて積層セラミックコンデンサー（MLCC）用材料の生産能力を増強する方向で検討している。設備投資の規模を含め来年3月までに判断する。矢倉敏行社長がインタビューで明らかにした。

堺化学では2025年末から電子材料の売り上げが急増、一部製品の受注は前年の2倍に増えた。現在では電子材料事業が稼ぎ頭となっている。

矢倉氏はAI関連需要について、「こんな伸びるとは考えていなかった」と述べた。注文は現在、生産能力の上限に迫っているという。

事業環境を踏まえ、同社は現在、必要な生産能力の増強幅を精査している。矢倉氏によると2桁%の規模になる可能性もある。

MLCCメーカーは通常、バリウムとチタンの化合物を混合し、焼成・粉砕することで材料を自社生産している。ただ、AIサーバー向けなどに使われる付加価値が高いコンデンサーの材料は堺化学に調達を頼っていると矢倉氏は説明した。

取引先のMLCCメーカーは、打ち合わせのたびに発注見通しを引き上げているという。ブルームバーグのデータによると、堺化学の顧客には村田製作所や太陽誘電などが含まれる。

堺化学の技術の源流は100年以上前にさかのぼる。同社は、かつて白粉（おしろい）に使われていた鉛白（えんぱく）に代わる安全な原料として、酸化亜鉛の製造を始めた。そこで磨いた微細で粒径のそろった粉末をつくる技術が、現在はAIデータセンター向けコンデンサーの材料に生かされている。

需要の伸びはやや鈍化しているものの、矢倉氏は少なくとも2027年いっぱいは現在の市場環境が続く可能性が高いとの見方を示した。

一方、需要が旺盛で生産能力が不足する中でも、投入コストの上昇分を超える値上げは考えていない。矢倉氏は、こうした価格政策が企業価値の重しになっている面も認めつつ、「まじめなんです」と語った。

item.title: フェアウエーから太陽光パネルへ、適地不足補うゴルフ場という選択肢
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 群馬県にある美野原カントリークラブ（中之条町）には、森林の間を縫うようにフェアウエーが続いている。しかし、数年後にはこの光景が何列にも並ぶ太陽光パネルの下に姿を消す。

太陽光発電施設を開発する上里建設（埼玉県本庄市）が2025年に取得した同ゴルフ場は、日本で広がりつつあるゴルフ場跡地のエネルギー利用を象徴するプロジェクトの一つだ。

政府は40年度の発電電力量に占める太陽光の割合を23－29%程度と見込む。2023年度は9.8%だった。一方、国土の多くを山地が占める日本では、大規模な太陽光発電（メガソーラー）に適した土地の確保が難しい。ゴルフ場が今では新たな受け皿になっている。

ブルームバーグNEFのデータによると、出力0.9メガワット以上の国内メガソーラーの設備容量の約9%をゴルフ場跡地の施設が占める。岡山県美作市にある国内最大級のメガソーラーも、かつてのフェアウエーが利用されている。

太陽光発電は、政府の支援策を追い風に拡大してきた。11年の福島原子力発電所事故後、原発の停止が相次ぐ中、政府は12年に「固定価格買取制度（FIT）」を導入。発電事業者の採算を支える仕組みによって普及が進んだ。

だが、15年をピークに太陽光発電設備の導入ペースは鈍化し、FITによる支援も縮小してきた。高市早苗首相も、太陽光発電への支援制度を見直す方針を示すなど、大規模施設を取り巻く事業環境は厳しくなってきた。

太陽光発電の拡大を阻む壁の一つが建設用地の確保だ。九州大学のカーボンニュートラル・エネルギー国際研究所のアンドリュー・チャップマン准教授によると、メガソーラーには十分な日照に加え、送電網に接続でき、住宅地から適度に離れた土地が必要となる。多くのゴルフ場はこうした条件を満たしている。

「平たんで傾斜も緩く、山地でないゴルフ場ならよい買い物だ」とチャップマン氏は指摘。「特に地方ではとても合理的な選択だ」と述べた。

item.title: 米軍が使う英空軍基地周辺でテロ計画か、5人逮捕－イラン関与も捜査
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英国の警察は27日、米軍も使用するフェアフォード空軍基地への攻撃を計画していたとみられる男5人を逮捕した。トランプ米大統領は、容疑者らが基地に「大きな損害を与えようとしていた」とし、攻撃を未然に防いだことを「素晴らしい」と評価した。

同基地は米軍の対イラン攻撃で重要な出撃拠点となっている。匿名を条件に語った関係者によると、英警察は、計画がかなり進んだ段階で阻止された重大な攻撃未遂事件とみて、動機の解明を進めている。

当局はイラン政府の関与があったかどうかも調べているという。ただ、捜査は継続中で、別の動機が浮上する可能性もあると関係者は述べた。

警察は当初、爆発物法違反の疑いで男5人を逮捕。その後、テロ行為を準備した疑いでも逮捕した。

与党・労働党の年次党大会でリバプールを訪れていたバーナム英首相は、今回の事件を「極めて憂慮すべきだ」とした上で、「地域社会を守り、国の安全を確保するため、政府は必要なあらゆる措置を講じる」と強調した。

英政府当局者によると、ストリーティング国防相は27日、ヘグセス米国防長官と電話会談を行った。フェアフォード空軍基地は、米空軍が欧州に爆撃機を前方展開する際の主要拠点となっている。

英国は現在、さまざまな安全保障上の脅威に直面しており、事件の動機として考えられるものは少なくない。

英政府はここ数カ月に起きた複数の反ユダヤ主義的な事件について、イランの支援を受ける勢力が関与したとの見方を公に示している。一方、イスラム過激主義に触発された脅威も高まっている。これとは別に、イスラエルによるガザでの戦争に反対する左派活動家が近年、英国の軍事基地に繰り返し侵入している。

原題：Trump Says Suspects in UK Incident Sought to Damage Shared Base（抜粋）

--取材協力：Ellen Milligan、Maria Paula Mijares Torres、Courtney Subramanian、Brendan Scott.

item.title: トランプ氏、イランとの協議は今週再開の見通し－アクシオス
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は、イランとの協議が今週再開されるとの見通しを示した。ニュースサイトのアクシオスが、トランプ氏との電話インタビューを基に報じた。同氏はホルムズ海峡の再開を巡るイランの最新提案を拒否していた。
アクシオスによると、トランプ氏はイランが求める合意内容について、1年ほど前なら米国は受け入れていた可能性があると指摘。イランは強気に出過ぎたとの認識も示した。
イランは27日、ホルムズ海峡の再開に向けた7日間の提案や、同国が提示したその他の要求について、米国からの最終回答を待っていると表明。トランプ氏がイランの最新案を拒否したことを受けても、条件を緩和する考えはないとしていた。
原題：Trump Says He Expects Renewed Iran Talks This Week, Axios

item.title: 台湾巡る米の立場、習主席の訪米後も変わらず－パーデュー駐中国大使
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領と中国の習近平国家主席は会談のたびに米国による台湾への武器売却について協議していると、米国のパーデュー駐中国大使は明らかにした。先週の習氏の国賓訪米後も、台湾を巡る米国の立場に変更はないと述べた。

パーデュー氏は27日、FOXニュースの番組で台湾に関する質問に対し、「われわれは独立を支持しないし、威圧も支持しない」と話した。

習氏は訪米中、中国が自国領と見なす台湾への支援を抑えるようトランプ氏に強く迫った。台湾独立に明確に「反対」するよう米国に求めた。習氏が台湾を巡る米国の数十年来の立場を変更するよう公に要求したのは初めて。

習氏に配慮するため、台湾が自衛に必要なものを米国が提供していないのではないかと問われると、パーデュー氏は「決してそうではない」と否定した。トランプ政権は既に台湾への110億ドル（約1兆7200億円）相当の米国製兵器の売却を承認しており、追加売却を巡る協議も続いていると同氏は説明した。

「会談ではトランプ大統領が習主席に米国製兵器を購入したいかと尋ねる場面もあった」とパーデュー氏は語った。

習氏4期目入りが見込まれる中、中国政府は民主主義体制で半導体産業の拠点でもある台湾を孤立させるため、外交圧力を強めている。中国は必要であれば武力を行使してでも台湾を支配下に置く方針を示してきた。

トランプ氏は26日、習氏とは台湾についてそれほど多くの時間を割いて話さなかったと述べた。その上で、台湾問題に対する自身の考えを習氏は「十分に理解している」と話した。

原題：US Policy Stance on Taiwan Unchanged After Xi Visit, Perdue Says（抜粋）

item.title: UBSとの統合に複数の大手銀行が関心、少なくとも8社－スイス紙
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 複数の大手グローバル銀行がスイスのUBSグループに対し、統合の可能性に関心を示している。スイスの大衆紙ブリックが事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。
世界の大手金融機関少なくとも8社がUBSに対し、協議に応じる意向を示したと、関係者の1人は話したという。同紙は、こうした意向がいつ示されたのか、UBSに関心を示した金融機関名については明らかにしていない。
UBSの広報担当者は「この件に関する臆測や見解」についてはコメントしないと述べた。
スイス議会上院では今月、国内最大の銀行UBSに対し、外国子会社を支えるための自己資本をさらに積み増すよう義務付ける案について、過半数の議員が支持した。
ブルームバーグ・ニュースはこれまで、UBSが自己資本規制を過度に厳しいと判断した場合、スイス国外への本社移転も選択肢として検討してきたと報じている。
原題：UBS Has Attracted Interest

item.title: ボーイング、737MAXのソフトウエア不具合を確認－認証などに遅れも
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米航空機大手ボーイングは、737MAXの航法システムに、着陸時のパイロットの作業負担を増やす可能性がある問題が見つかったことを明らかにした。最新型ナローボディー機の投入が遅れる可能性もある。

ボーイングは発表文で、「特定の着陸状況でパイロットが自動飛行誘導を利用できなくなる可能性があるソフトウエア上の問題について、737の全運航会社に先月通知した」と説明。「こうした状況に安全に対処するための既存のパイロット手順を再確認する情報を運航会社と共有した」とした。

米連邦航空局（FAA）は別途、この不具合が飛行の安全上の問題に当たるかどうかを判断するため、審査委員会を招集していると明らかにした。安全上の問題と判断されれば、ボーイングの新型737MAX10の認証が遅れ、最近承認されたMAX7の就航にも支障が出る恐れがある。

今回のソフトウエア不具合は、パイロットが着陸を中止する必要が生じた際に発生する可能性がある。ボーイングによると、その場合、自動操縦システムのピッチ制御がより簡易な自動化モードに切り替わり、通常のモードに比べてパイロットの作業負担が増える。

米紙ウォールストリート・ジャーナル（WSJ）は、この不具合と、ボーイングの認証スケジュールに影響する可能性について先に報じていた。

この不具合を恒久的に解消する対応は当初2028年に予定されていたが、ボーイングは実施時期の前倒しに取り組んでいる。それまでの対応として、737MAXを運航する航空会社のパイロット向けに通知を準備している。

原題：Boeing Identifies 737 Max Software Glitch That May Prompt Delays（抜粋）

item.title: 米にもAI管理の責任と中国メディア－合意履行の必要性も指摘
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国と米国にはAIを適切に発展させ、管理する能力と責任があると、国営中央テレビ（CCTV）系のSNSアカウント、玉淵譚天が27日の投稿で主張した。

習近平国家主席とトランプ米大統領がAIから貿易まで幅広い問題を協議するため、ワシントンで首脳会談を行った数日後に掲載された今回の論評は、習氏の発言として、米中はAIを人間の管理下に置き、人々に恩恵をもたらすようにすべきだと伝えた。

AIの発展には技術革新とその恩恵の共有が求められる一方、適切な管理には悪用や制御不能といったリスクへの対処が欠かせないとした。

論評はまた、すでに合意した事項を実行に移す必要性を強調。両首脳は、米中経済・貿易協議メカニズムの積極的な役割と、両国の経済・貿易チームによる協議の成果を評価した。これには、貿易委員会など枠組みの設置・推進、300億ドル（約4兆7000億円）の相互関税引き下げ措置での合意、マレーシア・クアラルンプールでの経済・貿易協議の成果の延長などが含まれる。各レベルの政府部門が双方の合意を着実に実行すべきだとした。

原題：China State Media Says US Shares Responsibility for Managing AI（抜粋）

item.title: Trump says men arrested at UK air base used by US were looking to do 'big damage'
item.description: Five men are held on terrorism suspicion after armed police stopped three vans near RAF Fairford, prompting evacuations and a bomb disposal search.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump says men arrested at UK air base used by US were looking to do 'big damage'

Five men are held on terrorism suspicion after armed police stopped three vans near RAF Fairford, prompting evacuations and a bomb disposal search.

B‑1B Lancer bomber is parked at the RAF Fairford airbase, which hosts United States Air Force (USAF) personnel, in Fairford, Gloucestershire, Britain, Sep 27, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Shepheard)

FAST

FAIRFORD, England: British police arrested five men on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences on Sunday (Sep 27) near an air base that has been used by the US to strike Iran, after a tip-off that three vans had been seen heading to the military airfield.

US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities.

British counterterrorism detectives leading the investigation said police had received a call about three suspicious vehicles that appeared to be travelling towards RAF Fairford in the west of England in the early hours of Sunday.

Five men were arrested by armed officers and later held on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act. Police, who said they believed the incident was now contained, have not yet publicly stated who they assessed was involved.

An Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely, a source familiar with the investigation said, while a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at.

Related:

US Treasury chief Bessent claims successes in isolating Iran

Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz proposal; Tehran calls for diplomacy

POLICE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND CIRCUMSTANCES "We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody," Counter Terrorism Policing Senior National Coordinator Vicki Evans said in a statement.

"As you would expect we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident."

Police said a 400m cordon was in place around the base as the bomb disposal unit investigated the vans. Local residents in 85 homes in a nearby village were evacuated and armed officers were patrolling the site.

The British government, which has given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz , said Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being updated on the incident.

Burnham thanked the police and armed forces, saying on X: "I know today's incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country".

Britain said in July its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned it not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target.

"The arrest in the UK was fantastic," Trump told reporters, saying it was "an amazing job".

"We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our fort and working with the British worked out great ... We had them under view for a long time, and we got them," Trump added.

On Sunday morning, the base was blocked by armed police while large machinery also prevented access, and Reuters witnesses said security had been increased at other bases used by the US, with armoured vehicles and soldiers at the gates of RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall in eastern England.

Emergency vehicles are parked at Fairford Youth Football club, near RAF Fairford airbase, which hosts United States Air Force (USAF) personnel, in Fairford, Gloucestershire, Britain, Sep 27, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Shepheard)

DECLARATION OF A MAJOR INCIDENT A local farmer told the Daily Telegraph newspaper she had alerted police after seeing the vans and men acting suspiciously as she drove home from a party.

"I saw a group of Middle Eastern-looking young guys running off through the trees. Some of them had masks or balaclavas on, and they all scattered ahead of us as we drove back past," she told the paper.

"Some of them ran into the fields, and some of them turned to run towards the air base ... I mean, you don’t see masked men running around at half one in the morning in the countryside near a secure air base and not have concerns."

Local councillor Tristan Wilkinson told Reuters there had been a recent security alert at Fairford and surveillance had been stepped up.

"So there was a specific threat about six weeks ago from the Iranians on this base. At the time, there was increased surveillance around the area," he said.

A spokesperson for the US Air Force declined to discuss specific force protection measures at the base.

"The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families," the spokesperson said.

British ministers have also previously briefed providers of critical infrastructure on the threat posed by Russia, with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks.

Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.

Source: Reuters/fh/fs

item.title: 米からの最終的な回答、仲介国通じて待つ－イランのアラグチ外相
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： イランのアラグチ外相は国営イラン放送（IRIB）とのインタビューで、同国が示したホルムズ海峡の開放に向けた7日間の計画を巡り、仲介国を通じた米国の最終回答を待っており、それを踏まえて決定すると述べた。

item.title: 中国の消費関連株、失われた10年－AIに資金集中、先行きも楽観できず
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国政府がAI重視の姿勢を鮮明にする中、同国の消費関連株は失われた10年の様相を呈している。

消費セクターは、好調なテクノロジーセクターとは対照的だ。MSCI中国指数の消費財サブ指数はこの半年で約18%下落し、約10年ぶりの安値圏に沈む一方、AI関連銘柄の比重が高いテクノロジー指数は2016年の水準の2倍超に上昇した。直近の決算シーズンでは、MSCI指数を構成する生活必需品企業の利益が市場予想を約50%下回った。

こうした低迷は、中国経済の偏りを示している。政府がテクノロジー分野での覇権を目指す取り組みは輸出拡大を促し、AI企業への資金流入につながっているものの、内需への波及は限定的だ。8月の小売売上高は前年同月比0.4%増にとどまった。

旅行や消費にとって重要な時期である国慶節（建国記念日）の大型連休後も、このセクターに対する投資家の悲観的な見方が和らぐ兆しはほとんどない。

上海ジェイド・ストーン・インベストメント・マネジメントのファンドマネジャー、チェン・シー氏は「今夏のデータで、消費が回復しているとの見方は否定され、なお輸出一辺倒であることが裏付けられた」と指摘。「市場では、それが他のセクターから資金を締め出す形にもなっている。投資家の資金はAIの恩恵を受ける銘柄にますます集中する一方、消費などのセクターは無差別に売られている」と話す。

中国の中間層の台頭が世界有数の成長ストーリーとしてもてはやされた新型コロナウイルス禍前とは様変わりし、投資家心理は冷え込んでいる。

長引く不動産不況や所得の伸び悩み、消費者信頼感の低迷で、消費関連株は投資先として魅力を失い、かつての楽観論はほぼ消え去った。消費を支える重要な柱である住宅販売の回復に向け、当局は政策支援を逐次打ち出してきたが、十分な効果は上がっていない。最新のデータでは、住宅価格の下落が続いていることが示された。

item.title: 社債に警戒信号、米国債恐怖指数が示す－スプレッド拡大リスクじわり
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 世界的に国債が売られる中でも、社債は比較的底堅く推移している。ただ、その強さは長続きしない可能性がある。

利回りの先行き不透明感を映す債券市場のボラティリティーが急上昇している。過去にはこうした動きが社債市場悪化の前触れとなってきた。個人投資家などが警戒を強め、市場から資金を引き揚げるためだ。

現時点では企業利益は堅調で、社債利回りが全般に上昇しているのも、力強い経済成長を一部反映している。ただ、インフレ圧力が強まる中、米金融当局は利上げに転じている。

マスミューチュアルの投資戦略責任者ケリー・コワルスキ氏は、金利上昇は時間の経過とともに景気を圧迫し、企業利益を押し下げる可能性がある一方、社債はすでに想定が多少外れただけでも影響を受けやすい水準にあると指摘する。

「利回りが高止まりし、不安定な動きが長引くほど、金融環境の引き締まりが進み、経済活動や企業の利益率、信用力への圧力も強まる」とコワルスキ氏は話す。

その結果、社債はいずれ国債を下回るパフォーマンスとなり、企業が資金調達時に支払う米国債に対する上乗せ金利（スプレッド）が拡大する可能性がある。

JPモルガン・チェースのナサニエル・ローゼンバウム氏らストラテジストは先週、債券・株式市場のボラティリティーの過去の水準に照らすと、米投資適格社債のスプレッドは現在より約0.07ポイント広い水準にあるはずだと試算した。

原油価格の上昇とインフレ懸念の高まりを背景に、この1カ月は債券市場全般で利回りが大幅に上昇している。米国債は主要年限の大半で利回りが5%を上回り、5年債利回りも2007年以来初めて5%を突破した。

それでも社債は相対的な底堅さを維持している。米投資適格社債のスプレッドは24日時点で77ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）と、月初から2bp縮小した。年金基金や保険会社など、将来の支払いに備えて運用する投資家は、利回りが上昇すると社債を購入することが多く、これが社債の相対的なパフォーマンスを支えている。

item.title: 【焦点】米雇用は9月も堅調の見込み、コスト圧力でも景気に勢い
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国ではコスト圧力が強まっているにもかかわらず、景気の勢いが増しており、9月の雇用は2カ月連続で堅調だったとみられる。

エコノミスト予想では、来月2日に発表される9月の雇用統計で、非農業部門雇用者数が約9万人増加すると見込まれている。前月は3月以来の大きな伸びとなっていた。失業率は4.1%にとどまる見通しだ。

最近の雇用が拡大している背景には、当然ながら景気そのものの強さがある。需要関連の指標は、旺盛な設備投資が続いているほか、個人消費も改善していることを示している。こうした状況を背景に、米金融当局は政策の焦点をインフレに明確に移すことが可能になった。

一方、30日発表される8月のインフレ調整後の個人消費支出（PCE）は前月比0.5%増加すると予想されており、この通りなら1年余りで最大の伸びとなる。

これには米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）が重視するインフレ指標も含まれる。PCE価格指数と、エネルギーと食品を除くコア指数はいずれも、8月に前月比で伸びが加速すると見込まれている。

投資家はこうした統計を受け、米金融当局が今月の利上げに続き、10月の連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）会合でも追加利上げに踏み切るかどうかを見極めることになる。現時点では、来月に0.25ポイントの利上げが実施されるとの見方が優勢だ。

ブルームバーグ・エコノミクスのアナ・ウォン、アンドリュー・サッチャー、エリザ・ウィンガー各氏は「2カ月分のデータを見る限り、7－9月（第3四半期）も消費は底堅さを維持し、実質消費は年率3%を超える伸びとなる見通しだ。個人所得は0.5%増（前月0.4%増）に加速した可能性が高く、消費を支えている」と分析した。

原題：US Hiring Appetite Is Healthy as Economy Powers Ahead: Eco Week（抜粋）

--取材協力：Brian Fowler、Laura Dhillon Kane、Monique Vanek、Robert Jameson、Piotr Skolimowski、Mark Evans.

item.title: クリーブランド連銀総裁、金利上昇の要因指摘－政府債務や利上げ観測
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米クリーブランド連銀のハマック総裁は、米長期債利回りの上昇について、景気見通しの改善や政府債務への懸念、連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）による追加利上げ観測が背景にあるとの見解を示した。
ハマック氏は25日、同連銀が主催したイベントで「複数の要因が作用していると考えている。経済成長を示す指標がかなり堅調で、そうした状況が続くとの期待が一つだ」と述べた。
「FRBの反応関数がどういったものか、どのような政策対応が必要になり得るかといった要素もある」とし、市場では米国の追加利上げが織り込まれていると指摘した。
同氏はまた、政府支出や膨らむ政府債務も市場関係者は注視していると発言。米政府は資金調達をAI関連プロジェクトと競う必要があると述べた。

item.title: Trump predicts Cuba and US will make a deal
item.description: Fuel shortages and blackouts grip Cuba as Donald Trump says the US can strike a deal with Havana without military action.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Trump predicts Cuba and US will make a deal

Fuel shortages and blackouts grip Cuba as Donald Trump says the US can strike a deal with Havana without military action.

A file photo of a general view of Havana, in Havana, Cuba, on March 17, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Norlys Perez/File Photo)

WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump predicted on Saturday (Sep 26) that the US and Cuba will reach an agreement and that he does not think military action will be necessary. "I would say that Cuba and us will make a deal. I don't think we'll need the military," Trump told reporters at the White House. The Trump administration has openly stated that its goal is to change Cuba's government. A US-imposed oil blockade implemented earlier this year has put the country under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and blackouts exacerbated by failing infrastructure. "We want to help Cuba," Trump said before departing for Tennessee. "We want to open Cuba up to our people."

In an address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, Trump called Cuba a failed state and said "freedom will be coming" to the island nation. The Cuban delegation walked out of the hall during that speech. Cuban foreign minister Bruno Rodriguez said at the UN later on Saturday that Cuba will always be open for dialogue with the United States. He did not reference Trump 's comments specifically. "We are open to commercial and business relationships with US companies, just as we are with any other country," said Rodriguez, while also strongly condemning a US trade embargo on Cuba. The US has maintained the embargo on Cuba for more than 60 years, and the Trump administration has been stepping up pressure after using the military in January to remove Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

item.title: 高市首相がトランプ氏と電話協議、中国巡る課題で意見交換－連携確認
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は26日夜に、トランプ米大統領と電話で約20分間にわたって協議し、中国を巡るさまざまな問題について話し合ったと述べた。

高市首相は電話協議後に首相官邸で記者団に対し、「経済安全保障を含む経済や安全保障など、中国を巡る諸課題」を中心にトランプ氏と意見交換したと説明。その上で、「日米の連携を確認した」と語った。

電話協議は、24日に行われた米中首脳会談の後というタイミングで実施された。首相はトランプ氏から同会談に関する詳細な説明を受けたと述べた。

ホワイトハウスはこれに先立って公表した米中首脳会談に関するファクトシートに、「米国と中国は第2次世界大戦で同盟国として共に戦い、勝利した」との記述を盛り込んだ。

首相は会見で、この点に関するトランプ氏とのやりとりを聞かれると、具体的な話は外交上差し控えるとして言及を避けた。

その上で、「日本と米国は今や最も信頼し合える同盟国となっている」との認識をトランプ氏に伝えたと説明。「共に地域、そして世界の平和と安定に貢献していくことを確認した」と述べた。

高市首相は昨年11月、台湾有事は日本の集団的自衛権を行使できる「存立危機事態」になり得ると国会で答弁。それ以降、日中関係は悪化している。

トランプ氏は日中双方とのバランスを取ろうとし、5月に北京を訪問した際にも、直後に高市氏に電話をかけ、習近平国家主席との会談内容を説明した。

item.title: North America is building rare earth plants faster than it is building rare earth engineers
item.description: Engineering degrees output is less than half the roughly 600 a year implied by DOE's estimate of need, and about a 15th of China's.
item.dc:creator: Frik Els
item.content:encoded:
North America is building rare earth plants faster than it is building rare earth engineers

Frik Els | September 25, 2026 | 2:40 pm Careers   Critical Minerals   Education   News   Africa   Asia   Australia   Canada   China   Europe   Latin America   USA   Copper   Rare Earth

Colorado School of Mines at sunset. ( Image: Connor Beekman )

On August 7, as US President Donald Trump hosted mining executives at a roundtable in Washington, representatives of all 14 accredited US mining schools attended a parallel Department of Energy workforce event . They left with the first serious federal funding for mining education in a generation, more than $180 million in total , part of a package of deals the White House put at more than $2 billion and Bloomberg tallied at $3 billion .

The biggest slice is a new DOE programme called PROSPECT (Providing Opportunities for Specialized Education in Critical Technologies), worth up to $100 million and aimed at doubling the number of graduates with mining, minerals and supply chain credentials within two years. DOE puts the country’s need at about 6,000 new mining engineers over the next decade.

The Department of War proposed another $81.3 million for three schools, with Colorado School of Mines in line for $32.7 million for a critical minerals innovation and commercialization hub in Golden, South Dakota Mines received $25 million for a scholars consortium with the University of Kentucky and Missouri S&T, and Johns Hopkins got $23.6 million for a recycling hub.

The PROSPECT funding notice is, however, “subject to availability of appropriated funds,” and Congress has yet to pass a single FY2027 spending bill, leaving the government on a stopgap that runs out on December 11.

The Department of War awards are also still listed as proposed. The only money moving so far is a $16 million PROSPECT Planning Prize  launched on September 14, which offers up to $1 million per school for plans to grow credential output within two years. Applications close on October 5. A GEM Consulting study found that public capital in mining increasingly comes with workforce conditions attached  and singled out the $180 million education line as money that “could ease workforce shortages affecting multiple projects.” Measured against the more than $10 billion already committed to US rare earths and magnets by Bloomberg’s count, the people side of the ledger is getting less than two cents on the dollar.

The NDAA provision is stuck in the Senate

The legislative route that put mining schools on the defence agenda this summer has gone nowhere since the House passed the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act by 216 votes to 212 on July 22. The bill authorises about $1.14 trillion in discretionary defence spending and carries the surviving core of Rep. Burgess Owens’ Mining Schools Act, now Section 1883 of the text passed by the House (numbered 1853 in the committee mark and in Owens’ own press release).

Section 1883 directs the Department of War to use Defense Production Act authorities to support workforce development in the mining, processing, refining and recycling of critical minerals through university partnerships, scholarships, tuition assistance and on the job learning. It also orders an assessment of whether certain awards should be conditioned on a company’s participation, which would make training a term of the contract.

The section authorises no money, and it is not the Energy Department grant programme with an advisory board that Owens’ release describes. That programme exists only in the standalone bill, H.R.2457, which has not had a markup since it was referred to the House Natural Resources Committee in March 2025. The Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration has been pushing a version of the bill since at least 2022 , when the number of accredited programmes had already fallen from 25 in the early 1980s to 14.

The Senate has neither taken up the House bill nor passed its own since a July 14 cloture vote on the motion to proceed to S.4784 failed 50 to 46, with Democrats objecting to the Iran war and the size of the bill. We could find no equivalent workforce section in the Senate text, and no conference has been convened. Congress has passed an NDAA every year for more than six decades, usually in the final weeks of December, which points to a vote after the November 3 midterms. In the meantime, the August package, which runs on existing DOE and Department of War authorities, has overtaken the bill.

Other measures announced earlier in the year have moved only on paper, including a May 29 presidential memorandum that approved critical position pay of up to $400,000 for as many as 400 federal roles recruiting investment and engineering talent, and the Office of Personnel Management turned it into a final rule on August 26 , but no hires under the authority have been reported. The Critical Mineral Mining Education Act (H.R.7021 and S.3612), which would fund a $10 million a year mining Fulbright through the State Department, has not moved since January.

The National Science Foundation’s Critical Materials Crossroads Engine , led by the University of Missouri Kansas City and selected in July for up to $160 million over 10 years, held its launch  at Kansas City’s Union Station on August 21. Only $15 million is committed for the first two years, with the remaining $145 million tied to milestone reviews. The launch materials list rare earth elements among the target materials alongside nickel, cobalt, lithium, graphite and gallium, but no rare earth separation track has been named.

A pipeline that shrank for decades

Only 14 US universities offer accredited mining engineering degrees, namely Alaska Fairbanks, Arizona, Colorado School of Mines, Kentucky, Michigan Tech, Missouri S&T, Montana Tech, Nevada (Reno), New Mexico Tech, Penn State, South Dakota Mines, Utah, Virginia Tech and West Virginia. Twelve universities, among them Berkeley, Columbia, Ohio State and Texas A&M, have closed mining programmes since 1985. US schools awarded 700 bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mining in 1981, a level never reached again, and according to SME mining engineering enrolment fell from nearly 1,500 in 2015 to fewer than 600 in 2023.

Estimates of how many graduates the system produces vary with the source, as South Dakota Mines says fewer than 170 mining engineers a year, the National Mining Association says about 200, and Reuters counted just over 200 undergraduate mining and metallurgical degrees in 2023. Federal completions data compiled by Data USA show 285 mining and mineral engineering degrees at all levels in 2024, down 5%, with Colorado School of Mines (60), Missouri S&T (46) and Arizona (24) accounting for nearly half.

On any of those counts, output is less than half the roughly 600 a year implied by DOE’s estimate of need, and Bloomberg puts it at about a fifteenth of China’s . Doubling output, which is PROSPECT’s goal, would roughly close that gap, although PROSPECT counts credentials and not only four year degrees.

Colorado School of Mines warned of a “grey tsunami”  three years ago, when it put the number of US mining workers expected to retire by 2029 at 221,000, more than half the workforce. The estimate, which goes back to a 2014 SME briefing and was restated this summer as “within three years” , remains the only national figure available, and every measurable trend since has pointed the same way. US mining employment fell 20.4% over a decade , 71% of mining leaders surveyed by McKinsey said the talent shortage is already blocking production targets , and only 11% of young people say they would likely work in mining while 70% say they probably or definitely would not .

Juniors feel the squeeze most, with junior geologists now charging $500 to $600 a day , rates that four years ago belonged to senior geologists. US projects already take more than 30 years to move from discovery to production, and a shrinking pool of experienced technical workers  is slowing the engineering studies that come before a mine is built.

Flynn says the money goes to the wrong end of the chain

In July, retired Gen. Charles Flynn, former commander of US Army Pacific, argued that the federal rare earth buildout was missing the mark . About 90% of the raw material mined domestically still goes abroad for processing, nearly half the mining workforce reaches retirement age by 2029, and federal funding goes mostly to large producers while bypassing junior miners, their service providers and training. A $200 million grant to a single company, he noted, still leaves an 18 month gap before offtake begins.

“The country needs to think in terms of industrial systems and not just a collection of announcements and grants,” Flynn said.

Two months later the August package has answered his call for training money but done nothing for juniors, as the Office of Strategic Capital loans announced the same day went to Niron Magnetics , Sunrise Energy Metals  and Sila, all companies past the exploration stage. His other proposal, modular processing plants on military land, is already under way, with four companies building on army bases  and $725 million going to Energy Fuels and $500 million to Phoenix Tailings. The Pentagon has spent about $1 billion on rare earths since 2020  and expects its own magnet needs to reach about 10,000 tonnes a year by 2030.

From January 1, 2027, US defence contractors may no longer use Chinese magnets, a rule that applies to a country that used about 48,000 tonnes of magnets in 2025 against 300 tonnes of domestic supply . Even US-subsidised output is still being routed east  because the domestic separation and metallisation steps needed to consume it have yet to be built.

New plants will need people to run them

USA Rare Earth broke ground on September 9  on a $1.2 billion magnet plant in Blacksburg, South Carolina, with 6,400 tonnes a year of sintered NdFeB capacity, about 490 jobs and commissioning from 2028. The workforce line in the announcement was $250,000 for Spartanburg Community College’s new SPARK Center, roughly 0.02% of the capital cost, at a company that has lined up $1.6 billion in federal support . MP Materials says its $1.25 billion magnet campus in Texas , pitched at more than 1,500 jobs, is now “officially vertical.”

Energy Fuels began building its $104 million White Mesa heavy rare earth expansion  in Utah on July 29, with terbium and dysprosium circuits due by the end of 2027, while its $1.9 billion purchase of German magnet maker VAC, which employs more than 1,000 people in Hanau, still awaits approval from Berlin . Buying a trained magnet workforce is one way to get one. Vulcan Elements this week won a US Army contract to supply magnets for drones , its tenth with the Department of War, from a North Carolina plant with 10,000 tonnes a year of planned capacity and about 1,000 jobs. Cyclic Materials opened a 25,000 tonne a year recycling plant  in Mesa, Arizona, 17 months after announcing it, employing “dozens” of skilled workers.

Building a plant does not guarantee it will perform, as Serra Verde in Brazil  has shown with recoveries of 20% to 30% during ramp up against about 80% planned. The operation, which USA Rare Earth absorbed this month, has both the ore and the equipment, and its troubles point to the kind of operating experience China exports least willingly. EnerVenue cited much the same thing this week when it dropped a $264 million Kentucky battery plant for China , pointing to the “density of hydraulics, pneumatics and automation specialists” there.

MP Materials sued USA Rare Earth in May , accusing its rival of a pattern of recruiting MP employees to misappropriate trade secrets on magnet production, a sign of how scarce that experience already is outside China.

China treats rare earth expertise as a strategic asset

By Reuters’ count, at least 11 Chinese universities and technical colleges run dedicated rare earth degree programmes , enrolling more than 500 students a year and supported by more than 40 specialist laboratories, while no comparable undergraduate degree exists anywhere else. China’s Ministry of Education added a Rare Earth Materials Science and Engineering major to the national undergraduate catalogue in 2024, first approved at Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology in Baotou, 150km from the world’s largest rare earth mine.

Chinese financial media reported in June that Jiangxi University of Science and Technology in Ganzhou had been approved for a second major, Rare Earth Science and Engineering, and this term the university started an innovation class in the subject led by Li Chaozhong, dean of its rare earth school. “In China, I used to hire kids right out of university and they’re immediately productive. Anywhere else I need to train them for three years,” Constantine Karayannopoulos, former chief executive of Neo Performance Materials, told Reuters.

Reuters reported last October that there are only a couple of dozen experts in rare earth separation and refining in the US, Europe and Japan combined, compared with thousands in China , and that Beijing had started to catalogue its experts to make sure they do not travel abroad. China has long banned the export of rare earth extraction and separation technology and added magnet making technology to the list in December 2023 .

On September 15, State Council Decree No. 841 took effect, allowing authorities to bar Chinese citizens from leaving the country  if they breach export control or technology trade rules, or if they “may endanger” national industrial or technological security. The decree sets no time limit on such bans and allows notice to be withheld on national security grounds. It does not name rare earths, but Chinese commentators told Asia Times  it is aimed at sectors where Beijing already restricts exports, rare earths among them.

China’s magnet shipments to the US fell 21% in August to 512 tonnes , and some US buyers have waited more than six months for export licences . US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday that the trade truce, which includes the suspension of China’s October 2025 rare earth controls, would be extended by two months to January 10  as Xi Jinping began a state visit to Washington, although Beijing had yet to confirm the extension. JL Mag, the world’s largest magnet maker, is meanwhile targeting 60,000 tonnes a year of capacity by 2028 , against MP’s planned total of about 10,000 tonnes.

The three years of training Karayannopoulos describes matter because MP’s Texas campus and USA Rare Earth’s South Carolina plant both commission in 2028, while a student who started a US mining degree this month graduates in 2030.

Allies are short of engineers too

The usual answer, that the US can draw on Australian and Canadian graduates, does not survive a look at those countries’ enrolment data. In Australia, first year mining engineering enrolments fell from 267 in 2012 to 34 in 2018, and at UNSW from 120 in 2014 to six in 2018. Adelaide’s undergraduate degree is gone, Monash no longer offers one, and geoscience degree completions fell 40% over eight years , according to the Australian Geoscience Council.

The Minerals Council of Australia expects nearly half the country’s mining engineers to retire within the decade, and Canberra’s answer has been migration rather than education, with a skilled migration plan released on September 17 that prioritises engineers, geologists and metallurgists.

Canada has the most rigorous forecast, with the Mining Industry Human Resources Council’s June outlook putting the cumulative hiring requirement from 2026 to 2035 at 246,422 workers against a gap of 65,712, and acute shortages possible as early as 2027. Mining engineering enrolment peaked at 1,431 in 2014 and was down to 809 by 2022, yet seat utilisation averaged just 56% between 2021 and 2024, which means the places exist but the students do not.

Dalhousie closed its programme in 2024, while Saint Mary’s in Halifax expected a first resource engineering cohort of 20 to 25 students this autumn. Ottawa is relying on a C$81 million workforce alliance  and scholarships, and the Young Mining Professionals scholarship fund grew by a third this year . The updated Critical Minerals Strategy is still pending.

Britain had five mining schools turning out more than 300 graduates a year in 1990 , but Camborne School of Mines paused the country’s last undergraduate mining degree in 2020 and relaunched it only in 2025/26 , and the UK opened a £25 million critical minerals fund in August  that includes a magnet hub with a skills element. In Germany, RWTH Aachen closed its MSc in Mineral Resources Engineering to new entrants from 2024/25, although TU Bergakademie Freiberg is going the other way with a new raw materials bachelor’s from 2027/28. The EU’s Raw Materials Academy aims to train 100,000 learners by 2030 rather than grant degrees, and the Critical Raw Materials Act contains no skills article.

Where the top schools are

The 2026 edition of the QS subject ranking for mineral and mining engineering, published in March and current until the 2027 tables arrive next spring, puts Colorado School of Mines on top with an overall score of 95.8, more than 11 points clear of McGill in second place, while the rest of the top 30 fall within a band of about six points. MINING.COM last ran the list in 2022 , when Curtin and Queensland sat second and third.

Source: QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. Chart: MINING.COM

The US, Australia and Canada hold 17 of the top 30 places between them, and all three have seen enrolment fall hard. China places a single institution, China University of Mining and Technology at No. 29, with the lowest employer reputation score in the table, a reminder that QS measures academic and employer reputation among a largely Western survey panel rather than graduate numbers or industrial relevance.

Missouri S&T produced the second most US mining engineering degrees in 2024 and does not appear in the top 30, while Imperial College London scores a perfect 100 on employer reputation at No. 8 even though its mining department no longer exists under its own name. Russia’s St Petersburg Mining University sits at No. 11, ahead of Toronto, Virginia Tech and Arizona.

Where enrolment is growing

Colorado School of Mines says undergraduate mining engineering enrolment has doubled in three years, from 101 students in 2023 to about 183 by May, and this autumn it launched a minor in mineral processing and extractive metallurgy aimed at critical minerals recovery. DOE’s latest $10 million round of critical minerals research funding  went partly to Mines and the University of Arizona, where the MiningWerx pilot processing hub has $3.85 million in federal and state money. The University of Texas at El Paso is recruiting its first mining engineering class for autumn 2027 with $52 million from industry and the state, targeting 100 graduates a year, roughly a third of current national output.

Companies are also building pipelines of their own, and Neo Performance Materials’ partnership with Tallinn University of Technology in Estonia covers joint curricula and internships and is the only formal rare earth talent pipeline of its kind we have found outside China. USA Rare Earth’s demonstration plant in Wheat Ridge, Colorado runs a multistage solvent extraction circuit with 28 engineers, scientists and technicians on rotating shifts, a useful measure of what each new separation line needs in people. MP Materials grew from eight contractors in 2017 to 998 employees at the end of 2025, which shows a well funded operator can build a workforce, although juniors and service companies do not have MP’s balance sheet.

What comes next

The August 7 package is the first time Washington has put real money into mining education, and it deserves credit for that, but it amounts to $180 million, most of it proposed or awaiting appropriation, against more than $10 billion committed to plants. Section 1883 authorises no money and sits in a Senate that has not taken up the bill, and the Mining Schools Act has gone 18 months without a markup. The plants commission in 2028, this autumn’s freshmen graduate in 2030 and UTEP’s first class in 2031 at the earliest.

The next test comes on October 5, when applications close for the PROSPECT Planning Prize and the number of schools competing will show how much capacity exists to scale up. Congress then has until December 11, when the stopgap funding bill expires, to decide whether PROSPECT’s $100 million becomes real money, and on January 10 the extended truce covering China’s rare earth controls is due to run out.

item.title: A Lapel Pin Fuels Chinese Talk of a China-Russia-Iran Triangle
item.description: In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one …
item.dc:creator: Rudy Lu
item.content:encoded:
In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one another — for clues about relationships that official readouts rarely reveal.

A brief encounter between the foreign ministers of China, Russia and Iran at the BRICS summit has become the latest example.

Video from the sidelines of the summit in New Delhi showed Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi chatting and laughing with his Russian and Iranian counterparts Sergei Lavrov and Abbas Araghchi. At one point, Wang reached toward a pin on Araghchi’s jacket, prompting the Iranian foreign minister to laugh.

Araghchi’s official Telegram channel later posted a close-up of the exchange , identifying the pin as an emblem depicting the map of Iran.

The moment quickly spread across Chinese social media, landing on the trending search list of Weibo, a Chinese social media platform often compared to X, under “Wang Yi helps the Iranian foreign minister straighten his pin” (#王毅帮伊朗外长整理胸针).

A wave of Chinese-language amplification followed.

Nationalist commentary account Rongping (戎评) described Iran as “holding the advantage” and in high spirits, with China and Russia sharing the mood.

“Such a personal and warm interaction between the Chinese and Iranian foreign ministers sends a strong signal to the outside world: China-Iran relations have long gone beyond a simple exchange of interests, and the two sides share a high degree of familiarity and trust,” it wrote.

Another online commentary said the seemingly insignificant gesture reflected a shift in the international balance of power that would make the White House “deeply uncomfortable.”

“U.S. pressure is pushing the three sides closer together,” it said. “Washington can continue to pressure the three countries separately, but it will find it increasingly difficult to stop them from exchanging resources, coordinating positions and jointly seeking alternatives.”

It said Beijing could keep channels open to Gulf Arab countries, and Moscow could draw on its close strategic ties with Tehran. Working through BRICS, the three could help Iran break its diplomatic isolation and avert a complete rupture with the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states.

Those interpretations, however, largely reflect one strand of domestic online opinion that is sympathetic to Iran and distrustful of the United States. Beijing’s official posture has been more carefully calibrated, especially ahead of Xi Jinping’s scheduled Sept. 24 meeting with Trump in Washington.

Araghchi traveled to Beijing on Sep. 16 for talks with Wang Yi. The Chinese Foreign Ministry described Iran as a “comprehensive strategic partner” and said Beijing was prepared to help safeguard Tehran’s “legitimate rights and interests.”

But much of Wang’s message focused on containing the conflict. He urged Iran and the United States to exercise restraint and return to negotiations, backed dialogue between Tehran and Gulf Arab governments, called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and warned against the fighting spreading toward Yemen and the Red Sea.

China’s balancing role was also evident when Saudi Arabia asked Beijing to press Iran to rein in the Houthis, Reuters reported, citing three Iranian sources . China then privately urged Tehran to use its influence over the Yemeni group, whose advances threatened Saudi oil exports and shipping through the Red Sea — a vital route for Chinese trade.

item.title: Rio Tinto to expand metals trading beyond own output
item.description: Mining giant targets third-party deals and derivatives as CEO Simon Trott seeks more value from its global asset base.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Jamasmie
item.content:encoded:
Rio Tinto to expand metals trading beyond own output

Cecilia Jamasmie | September 24, 2026 | 4:46 am Markets   Suppliers & Equipment   Top Companies   Asia   Australia   Europe   Aluminum   Copper   Iron Ore   Lithium

Rio Tinto produces alumina as a core intermediate step in its vertically integrated aluminum business. ( Image courtesy of Rio Tinto. )

Rio Tinto (ASX, LON: RIO) plans to expand its metals trading business into third-party material and derivatives as chief executive Simon Trott seeks to squeeze more value from the world’s second-largest miner.

The initiative, Bloomberg reported , would mark a shift for Rio Tinto, which has historically focused on marketing its own production and operates a much smaller trading business than Glencore (LON: GLEN).

Glencore’s extensive trading network was one attraction during unsuccessful takeover talks between the companies over the past two years.

Rio Tinto does not intend to replicate standalone commodity trading houses, but is considering a significant expansion of its existing commercial business under chief commercial officer Bold Baatar, according to Bloomberg .

The push could give Rio greater flexibility to profit from regional supply imbalances and spare capacity across its global operations while broadening a commercial business that remains modest compared with major commodity traders.

Trading opportunities

Rio Tinto is considering more third-party trading in markets where its existing assets could provide an advantage. That includes alumina, where the company has surpluses in some regions and shortages in others.

In North America, its Kennecott operations have spare copper smelting capacity, creating opportunities to handle additional material. Rio Tinto could also trade copper cathode and related products such as sulphuric acid.

The commercial team currently has about 20 traders and could add several more as the company expands the operation.

The strategy fits with Trott’s broader overhaul of Rio Tinto since he became CEO last year . He has laid out plans to simplify the company, sell assets, cut costs and improve returns.

Rio Tinto is also in talks with Dutch multinational Vitol Group over a potential freight and logistics joint venture, another move that could reshape how the miner handles its global supply chain.

item.title: Following the herd: The push to make beef deforestation-free
item.description: It is not often that an exposé by an NGO triggers legislation to be enacted in just five years, but Colombia has achieved exactly this with its cattle traceability law.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Early
item.content:encoded: It is not often that an exposé by an NGO triggers legislation to be enacted in just five years, but Colombia has achieved exactly this with its cattle traceability law. Cattle ranching is estimated to account for 80% of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest, and an investigation in 2025 by the US-based Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA) linked cattle ranching to deforestation in three of Colombia’s national parks in the biome. An earlier investigation in 2025 revealed that Colombian supermarkets purchased beef from ranchers illegally raising livestock inside national parks. Enacted in June, Colombia’s new law will require both the public and private sectors to ensure that their supply chains do not contribute to deforestation through a suite of measures, including deforestation-free certificates and ranchers installing devices such as ear tags and GPS chips on their animals. Though the legislation had a bumpy road to adoption – several previous attempts to get it signed into law failed – campaigners have been celebrating. Chris Moye, Latin American expert at EIA US, says: “It is basically the first national traceability system that, in theory, tackles the major driver of deforestation in Colombia.” Joao Gonçalves, global senior director for protein transition at campaigner group Mighty Earth said: “Ear tagging of individual animals is cheap and effective, enabling traceability from birth to market. Colombia is leading the way, and within two years its new law could make unprecedented progress in the fight against illegal deforestation.” Cattle is being taken to safety as smoke rises from forest fires burning vast swaths of the Chaco region, near Cadete Pando, Paraguay October 1, 2020. Picture taken October 1, 2020. REUTERS/Jorge Adorno Though the government has since changed hands, with Donald Trump-endorsed far right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella taking power in August, so far there has been no sign that new environment minister Fabio Arjona Hincapié is planning to unravel the law, Moye said. The Colombian government and private sector have six months from passing the law to finalise details of how traceability systems will work. Within 18 months, it must integrate databases across the different institutions involved in implementing the law, and within two years must implement due diligence policies and practices across slaughterhouses, cattle auctions, traders and live cattle exporters. Moye acknowledges that the deadlines are demanding. “It depends on the competence of the government, and the political will. That will be the key, and I guess we'll find out.” The president’s environmental policy platform makes no mention of cattle traceability and emphasises reducing regulatory burdens, which raise questions on how aggressively the government will implement the law, he notes. Nevertheless, the platform does commit to stopping agricultural expansion into forests and strengthening environmental institutions, he adds. And cost reductions in technologies that enable the traceability of cattle and to share information between institutions make the target dates more realistic, he says. Colombia’s two-year deadline to tackle beef-led deforestation in the Amazon contrasts with the slower timetable in Brazil, home to 88% of the Amazonian herd. MANDATORY TAGGING The country has a national plan to introduce mandatory tagging of cattle and trace all movements of cattle, but not until 2032. The Amazon state of Para, host of last year’s COP30 climate conference, announced in 2023 that it would implement the scheme six years early, and would come into force in January this year. Read more However, its governor Helder Barbalho later postponed implementation of the programme until December 31, 2030, following complaints by the state’s ranchers, says Fabio Medeiros, strategic cattle partnerships director at The Nature Conservancy (TNC). Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella speaks during a press conference at San Carlos Palace in Bogota, Colombia, August 25, 2026. REUTERS/Luisa Gonzalez “Of course, it’s a setback – everybody expected Para to move forward, really before the other states. But it brings Para in line with other states, and gives producers more time to adapt,” he says. Traceability pilots are under way in Mato Grosso, Tocantins, Rio Grande do Sul and São Paulo. Other work includes engagement with smallholders to enhance productivity, and building a national platform to connect the state programmes, he says. “This is part of the movement that will cut deforestation. We expect that the implementation of traceability, and producer awareness about deforestation and the importance of compliance, will help it to move forward,” he says. There has also been a delay to a scheme requiring Brazilian banks to help combat illegal deforestation. In 2023, the Brazilian Federation of Banks (Febraban) asked members to join a self-regulatory scheme where they would ask meat processors in the legal Amazon and Maranhao regions to prove their cattle purchases did not come from areas of illegal deforestation as a condition of receiving credit. The scheme was to be implemented by December 2025, but was delayed until the beginning of 2027, Medeiros said. It was argued that it was almost impossible for producers blocked from supply chains after farming on deforested land to be relisted in supply chains, explains Medeiros. Such producers should be required to solve the problem they caused by restoring deforested areas rather than permanently punished, Medeiros says. “If producers can come back to the formal economy with obligations, this is what moves the game. Because everything that is in the past, we need to solve,” he says. Despite the delay, the scheme has already increased awareness of the issue among producers and banks, he says. Cattle stand at plant of JBS S.A, the world's largest beef producer, in Santana do Araguaia, Para state, Brazil September 11, 2025. REUTERS/Amanda Perobelli Some meat processing companies have been getting behind traceability efforts. In February, Brazil-based MBRF (formerly Marfrig) announced that it had achieved 100% traceability of its cattle supply chain, including both direct and indirect suppliers, across all Brazilian biomes where livestock is sourced. The company has monitored its direct suppliers using satellite-based tracking and geo-monitoring technologies since 2010, then announced its expansion to full monitoring of indirect suppliers in 2021. It identified socio-environmental risk levels using mapping that integrates multiple databases and classifies municipalities according to risk. “This pioneering approach made it possible to establish priority areas and a structured engagement schedule with direct suppliers to obtain information about indirect suppliers across all biomes where cattle are sourced for our production units,” according to Paulo Pianez, director of sustainability and institutional relations at MBRF. Suppliers associated with any non-compliance are automatically blocked from new cattle purchases in the company’s system until “clarifications and corrective action have taken place”, Pianez said. Though the company declined to provide absolute numbers of suppliers blocked, it said that they represented between 15% and 20% of its suppliers. Nearly 4,500 farms have been reinstated after becoming compliant, MBRF said. JBS has supported the rollout of traceability in Brazil, supplying two million electronic cattle ear tags to small ranchers in Para, in partnership with TNC. However, in June the world’s biggest meat processor revealed that it was abandoning its climate change target covering greenhouse gas emissions released into the atmosphere by suppliers, which represent the vast bulk of the company’s environmental footprint. Jason Weller, JBS global chief sustainability officer, justified the move on the grounds of difficulties in controlling indirect, or Scope 3 emissions, 92% of which are generated by the livestock it buys, according to its 2025 sustainability report. But Mighty Earth’s Gonçalves called the move “defeatist”. “JBSs’ Scope 3 emissions and deforestation cannot be addressed without knowing where cattle have been throughout their lives; traceability is therefore not peripheral to JBS’s climate commitment, it’s fundamental to delivering it.” The meat giant has shown it is capable of change, having already delivered a batch of fully traceable, deforestation-free beef to one retailer in the state of Para, he said. But Mighty Earth continued to find recent illegal deforestation in JBS’s Brazilian beef supply chains. A man picks up a piece of meat in Carrefour supermarket in Sao Paulo, Brazil November 27, 2024. REUTERS/Amanda Perobelli “The three-year delay to the rollout of the state-led traceability scheme in Para is unacceptable. Companies like JBS don’t need to wait for ambitious policy action. They have the clout and resources to require full traceability now. And retailers must insist on nothing less,” he said. Supermarkets also show mixed responses on the issue. French chain Carrefour has committed to 100% deforestation-free beef sold across all brands, including throughout the indirect farm supply chain. It has traceability and compliance in place for fattening farms across all Brazilian biomes, according to a spokesperson. Though it still needs to expand traceability to the other upstream links in the supply chain, it had already achieved this objective for own-label branded beef by the end of 2025, according to Agathe Grossmith, Carrefour’s CSR director. However, Grupo Mateus – the third-largest supermarket chain in Brazil – has been slammed by Mighty Earth for sourcing from some of the companies and slaughterhouses most connected to destruction of the Brazilian Amazon. It ranked lowest in an analysis of leading retailers and meat packers in Brazil. A spokesperson for Grupo Mateus said in a statement to The Ethical Corporation: “Throughout its 40-year history, Grupo Mateus has continuously strengthened its practices in the areas of compliance, integrity, governance and sustainability. The company reaffirms its commitment to complying with applicable laws and does not condone illegal practices within its supply chain.” Despite the setbacks in Brazil, Medeiros of TNC is upbeat about the direction of travel. “I think this is a very, very positive movement,” he says. “Some years ago, people used to say, ‘oh, it’s just Uruguay and Australia’. Now it’s not just them – it’s also Colombia, Paraguay, Argentina and Mexico – this is a mainstream approach,” he says. This article is from the latest issue of Ethical Corporation magazine, on deforestation risk. You can download the digital pdf of the magazine by clicking here

item.content:encoded:
SK Hynix Is Eyeing Intel’s (INTC) Ohio Site. Why Micron (MU) Should Pay Attention

Habib Ur Rehman Tue, September 22, 2026 at 9:33 PM MST 3 min read

INTC -5.70%

SKHY -4.64%

MU -2.58%

Explore stocks on Coinbase Trading disclosure

Trading disclosure The above button links to Coinbase. Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading. Coinbase pays us for certain activity generated through this link. Prices displayed are informational. Learn more

SK Hynix is exploring something it has never done before: manufacturing memory chips in the United States. Reuters reported on September 16 that the Korean memory giant is discussing several possibilities with Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC ), including leasing part of Intel's long-delayed Ohio complex or forming a venture involving Intel and large cloud customers. SK Hynix said no specific plan has been finalized. For Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU ), the talks matter because one of its strongest strategic advantages is being the major U.S.-based memory producer while AI has made DRAM and HBM increasingly scarce.

SK Hynix May Move Into Intel’s $100 Billion Ohio Fab. Micron Has a Reason to Watch SK Hynix Could Give Intel Another Path for Its Delayed Ohio Site Intel has committed enormous capital to Ohio, with the broader project potentially reaching around $100 billion over time. Delays have pushed planned production into the next decade. A tenant or joint-venture partner could therefore help Intel share the financial burden of developing the Ohio site rather than relying entirely on its own foundry demand to justify the buildout.

That is the bull case. The bear case is that exploratory talks are a long way from revenue. Bringing advanced Korean memory production to the U.S. could face cost problems, technology-transfer restrictions and objections from Seoul. Intel still needs its core manufacturing roadmap to work. Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) sits on the other side of the equation. AI demand has pushed memory pricing and availability into a strong cycle, and Micron is already pursuing a large U.S. manufacturing expansion. More domestic manufacturing incentives and customer interest in secure supply support that plan. A successful SK Hynix move could eventually erode part of Micron's U.S.-supply differentiation. U.S. cloud companies would gain another potential domestic supplier, while additional long-term memory capacity could eventually loosen the market that currently supports exceptional pricing. Hedge funds loaded up on both chipmakers Insider Monkey tracked 138 hedge funds holding Intel in Q2, up sharply from 112 in Q1. AQR Capital Management held roughly 10.7 million shares after trimming its stake about 7%. Micron's count rose to 184 funds from 154, one of the stronger quarter-over-quarter increases among large semiconductor names. Coatue Management expanded its MU stake dramatically during the quarter.

Intel had about 152.2 million shares sold short as of August 31, roughly 3% of public float and 1.7 days to cover. The talks do not rescue Intel's foundry strategy or weaken Micron overnight. They do show what AI scarcity is doing to the supply chain. Memory manufacturing is becoming strategic enough that SK Hynix is considering putting advanced capacity on American soil, and Intel's delayed Ohio project suddenly gives it a potentially valuable asset to negotiate with.

Story Continues While we acknowledge the potential of INTC and MU as investments, we believe certain other AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe termine sans direction, prudence sur l'Iran
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe termine sans direction, prudence sur l'Iran 28 septembre (Reuters) - Les Bourses européennes ont terminé sur de faibles variations lundi, effaçant leurs gains observés plus tôt, la prudence s'imposant face à la pression sur le marché obligataire et les cours pétroliers après le refus par Donald Trump du plan de paix iranien. BCE: Une réponse mesurée reste appropriée pour juguler l'inflation, dit Lagarde Une réponse mesurée reste appropriée pour contenir la hausse des prix, a déclaré lundi la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, Christine Lagarde, l'inflation enregistrée cette année n'ayant pas encore entraîné d'effets de second tour dans la zone euro. TotalEnergies augmente ses rachats d'actions alors que les prix du carburant portent les bénéfices 28 septembre (Reuters) - TotalEnergies a annoncé lundi prévoir de racheter 2,5 milliards de dollars (2,20 milliards d'euros) de ses actions au quatrième trimestre 2026, contre 1,5 milliard au cours des trimestres récents, le groupe présentant sa stratégie et ses perspectives 2026 à l'occasion d'une journée des investisseurs à New York. Bill Gates appelle à son tour à mieux encadrer l'IA L'intelligence artificielle (IA) doit être encadrée bien au-delà d'un seul dispositif d'autorégulation, a déclaré Bill Gates, cofondateur de Microsoft, appelant le Congrès américain à adopter une législation en la matière. Le dirigeant d'Armani indique que la vente envisagée d'une part du groupe pourrait concerner plusieurs investisseurs Le groupe de luxe italien Armani est disposé à envisager plusieurs investisseurs pour la vente d'une participation de 15% prévue dans le testament du fondateur Giorgio Armani, a déclaré dimanche son directeur général, Giuseppe Marsocci. Airbus recule après un défaut de qualité sur des A321neo L'action Airbus reculait vendredi, l'avionneur européen ayant annoncé la veille avoir identifié un défaut de qualité susceptible d'affecter des centaines de ses appareils à succès de type A321neo. Le financement de l'IA fait peser des risques systémiques sur l'économie américaine selon une étude Le développement de l’intelligence artificielle devrait, à terme, mobiliser une part plus importante de la production américaine que ne l'avait fait le déploiement du réseau électrique, des chemins de fer, des autoroutes inter-États ou encore d’internet, avec une structure financière de plus en plus complexe présentant des risques potentiellement systémiques, selon une étude universitaire à paraître vendredi. Zone euro: La croissance des prêts aux entreprises ralentit en août, selon la BCE La croissance des prêts aux entreprises dans la zone euro a ralenti en août, montrent les données publiées vendredi par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). Allemagne: Le moral des consommateurs devrait se dégrader plus que prévu, selon GfK Le moral des consommateurs allemands devrait se dégrader plus que prévu à l'approche du mois d'octobre, montre une enquête publiée vendredi. ArcelorMittal prévoit une charge de $1 md après des frappes sur son aciérie de Kryvyi Rih en Ukraine ArcelorMittal a annoncé vendredi ne pas être en mesure de relancer l'activité de son aciérie ukrainienne de Kryvyi Rih, touchée par des frappes de missiles le 21 septembre, le groupe anticipant une charge de dépréciation hors flux de trésorerie d'environ un milliard de dollars (878,35 millions d'euros).

item.description: A Metz, séquence européenne pour le pape Léon XIV et Emmanuel Macron
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Metz, séquence européenne pour le pape Léon XIV et Emmanuel Macron METZ, Moselle, 28 septembre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV conclut ce lundi sa tournée en France par une dernière étape à Metz, non loin de la frontière allemande, pour une séquence dédiée à l'Europe et à la paix en présence du président Emmanuel Macron. Bombardements russes meurtriers sur Kyiv et Dnipro KYIV, 28 septembre (Reuters) - L'armée russe a de nouveau bombardé Kyiv lundi, visant plusieurs cibles dont le bâtiment de l'Académie des Sciences, dans le centre de la capitale, où le maire Vitali Klitchko déplore un mort et 19 blessés. Royaume-Uni: Cinq suspects d'un projet d'attentat contre une base de la RAF libérés sous caution FAIRFORD, Angleterre, 28 septembre (Reuters) - La police britannique a interrogé lundi cinq hommes suspectés de projet terroriste avant d'annoncer leur libération sous caution, au lendemain de leur interpellation près d'une base aérienne utilisée par les États-Unis pour mener des frappes contre l'Iran. Andersson dit ne pas pouvoir former un gouvernement, Kristersson revient dans le jeu STOCKHOLM, 28 septembre (Reuters) - La présidente du Parti social-démocrate suédois, Magdalena Andersson, a annoncé lundi ne pas être en mesure d'obtenir un soutien suffisant pour former un nouveau gouvernement après la courte victoire du bloc de centre-gauche aux élections législatives du 13 septembre. Le Rassemblement national aura un groupe au Sénat, une première PARIS, 27 septembre (Reuters) - Le Rassemblement national sera en mesure de composer un groupe au Sénat, soit au moins 10 élus, ce qui sera une première pour la formation d'extrême-droite, à l'issue des élections sénatoriales de ce dimanche qui a vu le renouvellement de la moitié des sièges de la Chambre haute du Parlement. Le pape Léon XIV a passé deux heures avec des victimes de violences sexuelles commises par des prêtres Le pape Léon XIV a rencontré des victimes de violences sexuelles commises par des prêtres dimanche, lors de sa visite à Lourdes, après avoir exhorté l'Église catholique à reconnaître ses défaillances et à panser les "blessures profondes" infligées en son sein. La moitié des sièges du Sénat renouvelée, le RN espère un groupe La moitié du Sénat français est renouvelée ce dimanche lors d'élections au suffrage universel indirect dont l'un des principaux enjeux est la capacité du Rassemblement national (RN) à constituer un groupe, soit au moins dix élus. Le pape Léon XIV parle "d'espérance" lors d'une messe géante au coeur de Paris Une messe géante au coeur de Paris a constitué samedi le moment fort du deuxième jour de la tournée en France du pape Léon XIV, accueilli sur l'avenue des Champs-Elysées par une foule nombreuse, joyeuse et recueillie. L'aéroport de Catane de nouveau fermé à cause des cendres de l'Etna Les vols à l'aéroport de Catane, en Sicile, ont de nouveau été suspendus samedi en raison des cendres générées par l'Etna, le volcan le plus haut et le plus actif d'Europe, qui avait déjà perturbé l'activité de l'aéroport plus tôt dans le mois et en août, a annoncé l'opérateur de l'infrastructure. A Paris, Léon XIV délivre des messages sur la paix, la fin de vie et le "paradis des machines" Le pape Léon XIV a délivré vendredi des messages de paix et de dignité humaine, s'inquiétant de "perdre notre humanité au milieu du paradis des machines" au premier jour de sa visite de quatre jours en France, "terre de riches racines chrétiennes".

Platinum Futures.PL1! **Platinum Futures** continues to present a constructive technical outlook, with the broader market structure favoring the upside. No specific entry level has been identified in this setup; instead, the focus is on the lower timeframe, where early signs of renewed buyer participation are beginning to appear. If this momentum develops into a confirmed bullish structure, the current phase could provide an opportunity to participate in the continuation of the broader trend.

**Key technical observations:**

• The lower timeframe is already showing signs of increasing buyer participation and improving demand. • The development of **Higher Highs (HH)** and **Higher Lows (HL)** would provide stronger confirmation of bullish market structure. • A constructive shift in the moving averages would further support the transition toward sustained upside momentum. • The absence of a predefined entry level makes confirmation of buyer control particularly important before considering participation in the next potential rally.

Technical analysis provides a useful framework for identifying momentum and market structure, while the broader outlook for platinum should also be considered through supply-demand dynamics, industrial demand, investment flows, and macroeconomic conditions. Combining these factors with valuation and risk assessment can provide a more complete investment perspective.

Precious metals can experience substantial volatility even within established bullish trends. Maintaining patience, waiting for objective confirmation from market structure, and applying disciplined risk management can help investors participate in a developing move without reacting prematurely to short-term fluctuations.

This publication reflects a personal interpretation of market structure and publicly available information. It is intended solely for educational and informational purposes and should not be considered financial advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any financial instrument. Independent research, prudent risk management, and personal due diligence should always precede any investment decision.
